newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - March 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - March 19.

text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Indonesian press on March 19. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

The Indonesian Meteorology and Geophysics office will issue a guide book on how to deal with earthquakes after a tremor shook capital Jakarta on Monday, sending people scurrying out of high-rise buildings and causing widespread panic. There were no reports of casualties but some buildings were said to have developed cracks.

President Suharto has criticised Indonesian social scientists for issuing what he called unsubstantial analyses of the unrest that rocked the country in recent months. He said it was rare to find analyses which could help clarify and settle a problem, adding that many of them were quick analyses with no strong basis and were not supported by strong facts.

The government has vowed to implement the new customs procedures on April 1 without any transition period. The new procedures include self-assessment on import duties and taxes, on-arrival inspections and post release audits. They will replace preshipment inspection system.

Hundreds of houses in Banten, West Java were damaged after an earthquake measuring 6.0 on the Ricther scale jolted the western part of Java island on Monday. There were no reports of casualties. The earthquake also shook the Indonesian capital of Jakarta.
